description:
Hey! I did Space Apps in 2024 and 2025, and I’m joining again this year. I enjoy turning space stuff into fun, visual projects. This time we’re doing the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge—telling stories about NASA gear left behind on the Moon and Mars in a way that feels cool and easy for younger people to get into.

We want to keep things chill, creative, and actually finish a solid project without burning out. Looking for people into storytelling, design/art, coding, video editing...
summary:
Keepers of Stardust is a 15-page illustrated digital storybook designed for children. In the story, four curious characters—Neil, Sally, Valentina, and Yuri—explore the inspiring journeys of real spacecraft, including Opportunity, Ingenuity, the Apollo 15 Lunar Rover, and Cassini. The project brings scientific discoveries to life through a warm, engaging, and imaginative narrative that young readers can easily connect with.

Making complex space missions and scientific concepts clear, accessible, and captivating for younger age groups is an important challenge. This book addresses that challenge by pairing the stories of real exploration vehicles with relatable characters, simple language, original illustrations, and real NASA imagery to keep children engaged and make learning enjoyable.

Fostering science communication and curiosity at an early age helps children see space not just as a distant dream, but as a real frontier shaped by human effort and a spirit of discovery. Both educational and inspiring, it supports future generations’ interest in space science.
details:
Keepers of Stardust: Stories from the Silent Explorers is a 16-page illustrated digital storybook designed for young readers (recommended ages 8–13), written by Bilgehan Pınar and Ecrin Biçer. The story begins in a rainy classroom where four students—Neil, Sally, Valentina, and Yuri—question why space history focuses on missions that have ended. Through a spark of imagination and golden stardust, they travel across Mars, the Moon, and Saturn, meeting four real NASA explorers: Opportunity, Ingenuity, the Apollo 15 Lunar Rover, and Cassini. Each spacecraft shares its real engineering challenges, discoveries, and final chapter in an accessible, first-person voice, followed by a dedicated closing page featuring real NASA photographs and mission highlights.

Rather than presenting space missions as dry timelines or disconnected machinery, the project turns past and completed space milestones into relatable stories of resilience, ingenuity, and scientific legacy. Young readers learn key facts—such as Opportunity’s 14-year journey and search for past water, Ingenuity’s 72 flights in Mars’s thin atmosphere, the Apollo 15 Lunar Rover’s wire-mesh wheels and Genesis Rock discovery, and Cassini’s 13 years around Saturn and Enceladus—while seeing how each mission paves the way for future exploration. Its intended impact is to spark early curiosity in STEM and space science, helping children view space exploration as an ongoing human story they can one day contribute to.

We designed and assembled the storybook using Canva, exporting the final project as a shareable PDF hosted publicly via OneDrive for frictionless access. All spacecraft photographs on the Meet the Real Space Explorers page are credited to NASA, and our scientific details are grounded in real NASA mission histories.

The creative core of Keepers of Stardust is reframing "completed" or "silent" spacecraft not as forgotten hardware, but as storytellers and pioneers whose journeys still guide new discoveries. In shaping the project, our team carefully considered age-appropriate language (ages 8–13), narrative pacing, visual engagement, clear structure with a table of contents and real-world reference page, and strict compliance with NASA image attribution and open-access submission requirements.
